resolution_caveats.collResSubset: `collRes` is a SUBSET of `resolved` — a resolved edge whose target has MORE THAN ONE declaration in the project, so production's own-file tie-break chose the row. It is NEVER added to `resolved`. The fleet's own indexer measures 37,318 of 49,729 such picks as WRONG, so this lane's resolved column is a FLOOR on correctness, not a count of correct edges; the per-row number is published so a reader can discount it rather than admire it.
resolution_caveats.ambKindSubset: `amb(kind)` is a SUBSET of `amb(decl)` (distinct KINDS among colliding declarations, where `amb(decl)` counts distinct DECLARATIONS), reported beside it and never added. The two are different numbers for the same edges, and only the by-declaration count is in the closure.
resolution_caveats.perProjectScope: THE RESOLUTION SCOPE IS PER PROJECT — the repository a file belongs to — which is production's scope (`parallel-indexer.resolveRelationships` fills `target_symbol_id` only from a project-scoped qualified-name exact match, or from a bare name whose count IN THAT PROJECT is exactly 1). A name declared in the corpus but in ANOTHER repository reads unresolved HERE and would not necessarily read so in a pooled scope; the arm prints both tables and this declaration publishes the per-project one as the verdict's.

resolution_caveats.partOfRelabelAndDangling: ★ `part_of` IS A 1:1 RELABEL OF include/require, AND ITS CLOSURE IS MEASURED IN THREE CLASSES, NOT ONE. The arm's TABLE 1 reads 1,494 `part_of` rows = 4 resolved + 68 unresolved + 1,422 extOK. (1) THE 1,422 extOK are rows whose `metadata.importProjectFile` FILE CLAIM the project CONFIRMED — the claim guard composes `__DIR__`/`__FILE__`/`dirname(__FILE__)` project-relative, refuses a path escaping the project, requires an admitted extension and `statSync`s, so a verified claim says THE FILE EXISTS IN THIS PROJECT. (2) THE 68 unresolved carry NO claim at all (claimKind "-" on every one): the target names nothing the project can confirm. (3) THE 4 resolved are ordinary name resolutions of a path-shaped target and are a coincidence of spelling, not a file binding. ⇒ A VERIFIED CLAIM IS NOT AN ADMITTED-POPULATION FILE: the guard admits an ON-DISK file (phpunit's untracked `build/.../vendor/autoload.php` is one), while the GIT-TRACKED population does not carry those trees — so the population census's `targetsNotInAdmittedSet` (1,492 of 1,494) answers a different question from the gate's claim count and the two must not be read against each other. ⇒ THE FOUR-WAY WRITTEN-FORM SPLIT IS MEASURED, not inferred: require 820 · require_once 662 · include 9 · include_once 3 (emission census `part_of.byWrittenForm`), and every row carries `metadata.partRole: "library"` because php has only the host form of Dart's two roles. The written form stays on the row as evidence; the relation is the file-inclusion fact.
resolution_caveats.partOfIsAFileRelationNotAModule: ★ `part_of` ROWS DO NOT CREATE A MODULE BINDING AND THE LANE PUBLISHES THEM ANYWAY. The included file's declarations join the includer's one global declaration space (a second declaration of the same name is a fatal error), which is exactly the contract's "a part shares the library's single scope, imports nothing" — so the relation is the file-inclusion fact and NOT an import. The `imports` ImportInfo directive list is still published (it is persisted into `brain_import` by src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts), and the LSP file-level readers already admit `part_of` as a dependency kind (`graph_request.ts`, `graph_usages.ts`, `evidence_tier.ts`), so no product surface loses the include when the stored label moves.
